pipeline_name: New Administration Capital PS Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: Keep as a distinct row (existence + classification hold up); the Status/Cost ref check failures are just verifier string-matching against a spelled-out Arabic number, not a real problem with the source.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's sole source, petro-news.com/95212/ (an achievements-style roundup titled '39 projects.. map of natural gas projects in Egypt', dated 2024-10-10), lists this exact project as item #23, titled 'Khatt Taghdhiya Mahattat Kahraba' al-'Asima al-Idariya' (feed line for the New Administrative Capital power station): the text reads (in translation) 'the project comes as part of the urgent plan to supply the Siemens power station with natural gas, via a 32-inch feed line, 63 km long, at a cost of 327 million EGP.' That is an exact match on length (63 km), diameter (32 in) and cost (327M EGP) to the GEM row, and it is explicitly framed as an URGENT/interim measure to get gas to the Siemens-built New Capital combined-cycle plant. Re-verified live: url_verifier OK 200, page text contains '63'/'32'/'327'. GASCO (the Egyptian Natural Gas Company) is independently confirmed via a live, verified source (youm7.com, 2016-04-03) to be the entity building gas feed lines plus pressure-reduction/measurement stations for exactly the New Capital / Beni Suef / Burullus Siemens mega power plants (~3bn EGP investment program), which supports this being a genuine GASCO grid-reinforcement project rather than a phantom entry. PipelineType=transmission is reasonable for a 32in/63km trunk-grade line even though its sole consumer is one power plant -- consistent with how GEM already classifies sibling New-Capital feed lines (P3930 Dahshur-New Capital 70km/32in, P3366 Tineh-Abu Sultan-New Capital 165km/42in). Status=operating is not literally stated in the source (no explicit 'operational' wording), but the article is an achievements/completed-projects roundup (published 2024, describing the project in the past/completed tense with a fixed final cost), and the New Capital plant itself has been commercially operating since roughly 2019, so 'operating' is a reasonable read -- flagging as a caveat rather than upgrading to a hard confirm. Fuel=Gas and Location=Egypt/Egypt are trivially correct. Overall tier=medium: one detailed, on-point, live source with an exact 3-way numeric match (length+diameter+cost), but no second fully independent source reproduces the same 63km/327M-EGP figures -- everything else found describes the sibling 70km/605M-EGP Dahshur line instead (see the duplicate-adjacent finding below).

validity.recommendation: Research and likely correct Owner1 from 'General Petroleum Co' to GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company) -- or whichever GASCO-family entity actually built/owns this line -- with a properly verified source naming the owner of THIS specific 63km line before applying.
validity.researcher_notes: The current ref (petro-news.com/95212, item #23) does NOT name an operator/owner for this pipeline at all -- confirmed by direct re-read of the source text around item 23; General Petroleum Co is mentioned only ELSEWHERE in the same article, attached to unrelated field-development items, never tied to this line. General Petroleum Co (the Arabic 'al-Sharika al-'Amma lil-Bitrol', GPC) is an EGPC upstream field-operations subsidiary (Gulf of Suez / Eastern Desert oil and gas production), not a national gas-transmission-grid builder -- implausible as the owner of a 32in trunk line feeding into the national grid for a mega power plant. Independent, live-verified evidence (youm7.com, 2016-04-03, headline translates to 'GASCO begins implementing gas lines for the New Administrative Capital, Beni Suef, and Burullus power stations') confirms GASCO is the company implementing gas pipelines plus pressure-reduction/measurement stations to feed exactly the New Administrative Capital, Beni Suef and Burullus Siemens mega power plants (about 3bn EGP investment, 2-year build). A search-engine-cached almalnews.com corporate write-up of GASCO's own project list separately named a project matching this exact title ('feed line for the New Administrative Capital power station') as one of GASCO's own notable lines, alongside -- and distinct from -- the Tineh/Capital line, which is consistent directional evidence; however that URL is now dead (404 on re-check with curl and url_verifier) so it is NOT proposed as a ref. No source found supports General Petroleum Co as owner of this or any comparable New-Capital feed line. Tier=medium: the owner correction is well-supported directionally by a live source on GASCO's general role, but no source pins GASCO specifically as owner-of-record for THIS 63km segment, so don't auto-apply -- flag for a follow-up owner search before the Update pass touches the operators/owners tab.

validity.recommendation: Human review: compare P7574 against P3930 (New Administrative Capital-Dahshur Gas Pipeline, 70km/32in) before treating both as final. Current evidence leans toward these being two genuinely distinct GASCO projects, not a double-count, but the resemblance is close enough to flag rather than silently pass.
validity.researcher_notes: The same source article (petro-news.com/95212) lists, only 3 items apart, two separate-looking projects both aimed at feeding gas to the SAME Siemens power plant with the SAME 32in diameter: item #20, 'New Capital-Dahshur "Siemens" line' (70km, 32in, 605M EGP) = GEM row P3930; and item #23, this row (63km, 32in, 327M EGP), explicitly framed as an urgent/interim feed line. A dedicated official presidency.eg project page exists specifically for the item-20/Dahshur line (url_verifier: 200, live), which is some evidence the 70km line is a distinct, separately-documented government project -- but I found no equivalent standalone official page for the 63km line to symmetrically confirm ITS separateness. A (now link-rotted, non-citable) GASCO corporate-news snippet did list the exact-titled 'feed line for the New Administrative Capital power station' and the Tineh/Capital line as separate entries in GASCO's own project list, which supports two distinct lines, but I cannot re-cite it (404 on re-check). Net: I could not fully rule out that '63km/327M EGP' and '70km/605M EGP' describe the same physical tie-in at two different reporting stages (e.g. a preliminary estimate vs. an as-built figure), especially since a separate GASCO 2020 annual-report mention cites 'new lines added in 2020: 72km total' -- close to, but not identical to, either figure -- which is as consistent with normal Egyptian-press rounding noise across sources as it is with two real lines. Recommend a human check GASCO's own tender/completion records before either merging or fully clearing this pair.

routes.start_name: Unnamed national-gas-grid tie-in point (not specified in any source found; the source only calls it a 'feed line' -- possibly a lateral off the Greater Cairo / Dahshur-area gas network given the sibling Dahshur-New Capital line's 70km route, but this is NOT confirmed for this specific 63km line)
routes.end_name: New Administrative Capital Power Station (Siemens H-class combined-cycle plant, approx. 4,800 MW; located on the Cairo-Ain Sokhna road about 42 km from Qattamiya, New Administrative Capital, Cairo Governorate)
routes.corridor_desc: Only the destination is well described in sources (New Administrative Capital power station, sited ~42km from Qattamiya along the Ain Sokhna road -- presidency.eg, live/verified), but I found no source naming the origin/tie-in point or the corridor the 63km line itself follows. Given the plant sits ~42-45km from central/southeast Cairo, a 63km feed line is geometrically consistent with a route from somewhere in the greater Cairo / Helwan / Dahshur gas-network corridor (the same general area the sibling 70km Dahshur-New Capital line starts from), but I cannot confirm this is the same corridor, a parallel corridor, or a shorter tap closer to 10th of Ramadan / Badr City. Do not treat this as more than a loose bound.
routes.researcher_notes: No coordinates fabricated: I could not find sourced lat/lon for either endpoint (the openinframap.org and power-technology.com profiles for this plant did not surface exact coordinates in what I could fetch), so both are left null with a word description only. Only the destination (the power plant) is reasonably well-anchored in words; the origin/corridor is unknown. suggested_route_accuracy is 'low' rather than 'medium' because only one endpoint is even loosely pinned.

summary: P7574 (63km/32in feed line to the New Capital power station, source petro-news.com/95212 item #23) checks out on existence/classification/spec (medium tier, single strong on-point source, no second independent corroborator for the exact 63km/327M-EGP figures) but Owner1='General Petroleum Co' is unsupported and very likely wrong (independent evidence points to GASCO); also flagging a low-tier duplicate-adjacent concern vs. sibling P3930 (Dahshur-New Capital 70km/32in, same source article, same target plant) for human review. Route: only the power-station endpoint is nameable (Ain Sokhna road, ~42km from Qattamiya); origin/corridor unsourced -- suggested_route_accuracy=low, no coordinates fabricated.
